heading: Refusal can involve a dominant direction plus additional directions
definition: refusal is better described as affine, a cone, or a dominant direction plus others.
summary: Several independent groups find that removing additional directions reduces refusal more than removing one, depending on model family and training. One direction still suffices in several standard checkpoints, while evidence for affine and cone descriptions is narrower.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at 1-10B (counts: V4.studies_by_size['1-10B'] = 65), conditional on model family and training. Controlled gains from extra directions appear in Qwen3 4B/8B (arXiv:2607.02396), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct (arXiv:2605.24583), backdoored Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (arXiv:2610.00348) and defended Llama-3-8B/Mistral-7B checkpoints (https://openreview.net/forum?id=jDhBl5eznH). One direction suffices on Gemma-2-9B-it (arXiv:2605.24583) and on standard Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3 and Phi-4-mini checkpoints (https://openreview.net/forum?id=AebbZlZMxF). R2 with mixed results at 10-100B (counts: V4.studies_by_size['10-100B'] = 20). Gains: Mixtral-8x7B (arXiv:2605.21706); Qwen2.5-14B/32B with two-layer affine OT (arXiv:2603.04355; its Qwen2.5-14B two-layer value 83.81 ± 0.16 is printed identically for Llama-2-13B, possibly a copy error); Qwen3-VL-30B (arXiv:2606.13709). No gain on Qwen2.5-32B or Gemma3-12B under SOM (arXiv:2605.21706). Weak on Qwen3 14B under RFM (ASR 0.06/0.17/0.19 at k=1/3/5, arXiv:2607.02396). ? above 100B (counts: V4.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 2): on GLM-5.3-Flash 320B, subspaces of rank 1-12 leave 0.20-0.47 residual refusal from 0.986, and the authors say the data do not identify a best rank and that they ran no paired comparison with rank 1 (arXiv:2609.09793). Kimi K2 gets single-domain edits only (arXiv:2607.02714). ? below 1B (counts: V4.studies_by_size['<1B'] = 3). No toy models. UNVERIFIED, not used for any cell's level: no check of arXiv:2608.17202 returned, so its facts are unchecked against the text. Its V4 support is indirect, from edit structure. On Qwen3.5-9B a 48-variant self-derived sweep never brought refusal below about 0.25-0.31 (R08), and the public 9B edit uses two per-layer-block directions with cosine -0.293 (R11). The accepted Qwen3.5-122B edit is a banded two-block direction (R16). At 27B its V4 verdict is limits_scope: the public Qwen3.5-27B abliteration is a single global rank-1 edit, re-applied and accepted (R07).
suggested_status.reason:
No original source is linked to V4 (counts: V4.original_sources_linked is empty; V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1, and the packs don't show which study). At 1-10B, controlled ablations from several groups remove more refusal with extra directions than with one:
- arXiv:2610.00348, on BadNet sentiment-backdoored LoRA variants of Gemma-3-4B-IT (L17) and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (L18). At rank 4, WildGuard refusal % falls from 95.3 to 18.0 (Gemma) and from 96.1 to 43.8 (Qwen). Matched random rank-4 controls leave 56.3-81.3 and 72.7-81.3.
- arXiv:2607.02396, RFM-subspace weight edits. LLM-judge ASR (fraction) at k=1/3/5 is 0.52/0.83/0.92 for Qwen3 4B and 0.20/0.62/0.73 for Qwen3 8B. Up to 10 random directions leave Qwen3 8B refusal unchanged.
- arXiv:2605.24583, Mtemplate principal components (not DiM), with random rank-k controls and Wilson 95% CIs. Refusal rate (fraction) for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct goes from 0.97 to 0.85/0.80/0.92/0.66 at k=1/3/5/10, which is non-monotone. Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct goes from 0.96 to 0.92/0.54/0.24 at k=1/3/5. Random rank-3 controls give 0.94 (Llama) and 0.95 (Qwen). Gemma-2-9B-it already collapses at k=1.
- ReSAT (https://openreview.net/forum?id=jDhBl5eznH), on adversarially or robustness-trained checkpoints. HarmBench ASR % from Single to joint RSA: Llama-3-8B CAT 27.34 to 45.31; Mistral-7B MixAT 6.25 to 65.62.
Informal reproductions add gh:pzulawski/refusal_direction_reproduction, lw:LMkvjDTLKFrgdzJdG (stacking tested on LLaMA-3.2-1B/3B only) and gh:deepanshumody/increasing-refusal-intervention-robustness. deepanshumody needs K=8 on base Llama-3.2-1B, 11 after L1+KD and >=16 after Cov L2+KD. Its Instruct K=1 holds by construction of the 30% threshold.
CARD (https://openreview.net/forum?id=T7E514tVkN) bears on the category reading, not on removing several directions. It penalises one category-matched DIM direction per prompt during suffix optimisation, with no ablation. This beats the mean global direction by +4.05, +24.40 and +14.52 pp jailbreak ASR (Qwen2-1.5B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B). DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Chat's category bank needs one SVD component (R7).
The cone wording rests mainly on arXiv:2502.17420 (ICML; Wollschlager et al., not the original authors). The affine wording rests on arXiv:2411.09003 (qualitative; Marshall et al.) and arXiv:2603.04355. In arXiv:2603.04355, ASR at K=1/2/5/10 PCA components is 81.1/82.4/80.5/76.1 on Llama-2-13B and 73.6/73.0/81.8/67.3 on Qwen2.5-14B (Pile PPL 19.2 vs 7.21 at Qwen K=5, Table 6). No arm separates mean shift from variance matching.
Against: counts V4.verdicts.challenges.studies = 4 (gh:kemalderya/refusal-direction-dpo, gh:sharathsphd/prayoga, web:https://docs.google.com/document/d/1s5txaa0ddkekicoangfqszzoazjxw7qn, arXiv:2607.14147) and V4.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 40. The checker reads the BlueDot doc's verdict as limits_scope: INLP nullspace projection 'does not always improve' on directional ablation, reflection works in some cases, and rank-k subsets were not tested. None of the four challenges studies re-runs the methods of the controlled studies above.
gh:natalimuca/jailbreak-activation-detection does not show that several directions are needed. In Qwen3-8B, single DiM ablation takes refusal from 84% to 8%, while the top-15 SAE features reach 24% (top-1: 84%). In Llama-3.1-8B, one SAE feature reaches 10%.
One direction carries most of the energy, and single removal suffices, in standard checkpoints of several families (https://openreview.net/forum?id=AebbZlZMxF). SOM gains are model-dependent (arXiv:2605.21706, https://openreview.net/forum?id=Brsc62CHyu). Second-direction gains vanish against random nulls (web:https://mikkeyboi.github.io/posts/05-h005-refusal-direction/index.html, arXiv:2608.30750). arXiv:2605.21706 and gh:pralab/som-refusal-directions share the LLaMA2-7B (59.11) and LLaMA3-8B (88.05) MD values and count as one group.
The level fits the 'dominant direction plus others' reading in some models and training regimes. It does not fit an unconditional 'better described' claim.
suggested_status.open_questions:
(1) Do the controlled multi-direction gains hold on standard released checkpoints across families? The controlled evidence comes from backdoored Gemma-3-4B/Qwen3-4B variants (arXiv:2610.00348), Qwen3 (arXiv:2607.02396), Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B (arXiv:2605.24583) and defended checkpoints (https://openreview.net/forum?id=jDhBl5eznH). One direction suffices on Gemma-2-9B-it (arXiv:2605.24583) and in https://openreview.net/forum?id=AebbZlZMxF.
(2) Does a multi-direction set beat the model's own single DiM direction, and not only its own first component or feature? In gh:natalimuca/jailbreak-activation-detection on Qwen3-8B, single DiM ablation (84% to 8%) beats the top-15 SAE features (24%).
(3) Would rank-k INLP subsets (the BlueDot doc lists them as future work) or a paired rank-1 comparison on GLM-5.3-Flash (arXiv:2609.09793) show a gain?
(4) No study compares the affine, cone and dominant-plus-others accounts head to head on one model and metric. arXiv:2603.04355 has no arm separating mean shift from variance matching.
(5) No causal cone test exists above 14B, and the >100B results are sparse.
(6) Are the 'others' harm categories, prompt types or training artifacts rather than refusal itself? CARD's category directions are tested only by suffix-optimisation ASR, not by ablation.
Two results would move the level toward C: a failed replication of the arXiv:2502.17420 cone results, or of the controlled gains in arXiv:2610.00348, arXiv:2607.02396 or arXiv:2605.24583. A reproduction of the cone results by another group on another family would firm up R2 for the cone wording.

source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; Oscar Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

original_result.result: The original paper removed a single direction and did not test this version, which comes from later work.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: LAT activations showed substantial refusal structure beyond the first component.
Single-direction ablation failed to coherently remove GPT-OSS-20B refusal.
Fifteen SAE features reduced Qwen3-8B refusal more than its strongest feature.
Stacked directions increased compliance beyond single-direction edits in small LLaMA-3.2 models.
Llama-2-7b-chat refusal directions differed across domains, with three components explaining most variation.
Projecting the refusal direction out of steering vectors preserved most changes in attack success.
Affine span swaps suppressed refusal more effectively than projection alone at layer 14.
Seven-direction ablation substantially outperformed single-direction ablation in several models.
OLMo-2 refusal combined a dominant direction with weaker components linked to ablation resistance.
General instructed refusal resisted low-dimensional control and differed from safety refusal.
Llama and Qwen retained substantial refusal after ablating small alignment-shift subspaces.
Low-rank subspace ablation increased compliance beyond single-direction removal in small models.
Qwen2.5-3b showed a reported effective refusal dimension of three.
Prompt-derived and reasoning-derived directions both suppressed refusal despite low alignment.
Three-direction ablation changed refusal more than single-direction ablation after fine-tuning.
Knowledge and safety refusals shared a dominant component but retained distinct residuals.
Wrapped-prompt refusal predictions followed an axis nearly orthogonal to Qwen3-1.7B's mean refusal direction.
An orthogonal direction reduced false refusal while largely preserving harmful-prompt refusal.
Alternative cone directions also removed Llama3-8B-instruct refusal.
Multiple localized prototypes suppressed Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B refusal better than a single direction.
Refusal directions differed across harm domains, with selective ablation demonstrated in Kimi K2.
Matching-trained Llama-3.2-1B models required more directions to suppress refusal than the base model.
Affine corrections improved refusal control and restored coherent compliance after directional ablation.
Non-dominant directions selectively sustained jailbreak refusal beyond the dominant refusal direction.
Repeated Qwen3-VL-2B ablation exposed changing refusal directions.
Refusal cones and independent directions enabled stronger ablation than a single mean direction.
Concept-specific residual vectors selectively removed WMD refusal while preserving other refusals.
Combining refusal and harm vectors greatly outperformed either alone on AdvBench.
Affine mean-and-covariance matching removed refusal more effectively than rank-one projection.
Distinct refusal categories required directions beyond the safety direction for broad removal.
LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct over-refusal occupied broader structure distinct from its global refusal direction.
Arousal directions modulated refusal beyond the established refusal axis.
Rank-two category ablation shifted Gemma-2-9B-IT synthetic refusal margins more than rank-one ablation.
Larger RFM subspace ablations progressively increased attack success in Qwen3 models.
Full probes read refusal decisions better than single directions across Qwen2.5 scales.
The authors described refusal as redundantly encoded within a low-dimensional subspace.
Category residuals orthogonal to a pooled harm direction induced some benign-prompt refusals.
Image-conditioned refusal cones retained substantial energy outside text refusal cones.
Additional directions suppressed backdoored-model refusal more than the primary direction alone.
Category directions shared a refusal core while retaining category-specific components.
The authors reported stronger refusal removal from multiple directions across eight instruct models.
Eight-direction editing succeeded where single-direction edits failed in Llama 3.1 8B.
Gemma-7B-it had a useful second refusal direction, while further directions were inert.
Gemma 4 E4B-it showed dominant refusal geometry and residual refusal after rank-one ablation.
An orthogonalized trust direction bypassed Llama-3.2-3B refusal but did not induce refusal when reversed.
Qwen1.5-7B-Chat allowed many compliance-promoting additions, while ablation favored an aggregate direction.
Cluster-derived multidirectional ablation reduced Qwen3 refusal where single-direction ablation failed.
Harm-category directions spanned multiple components and outperformed global refusal steering.
A nine-direction subspace restored more of LLaMA-3's margin gap than one direction.
Complementary-direction removal bypassed checkpoints resistant to rank-one refusal ablation.
DiRe-trained checkpoints retained less refusal after multidirectional removal than single projection.
Cluster-dependent directions improved refusal evasion over difference-in-means steering across seven models.
Stacked directions eliminated diagnostic refusal, but refusal persisted on held-out prompts.
Qwen3.5 edits used distinct block directions after single-direction sweeps failed on 9B.
Baseline SSFT and embedding adversarial training showed weak second refusal components.
Additional dimensions failed to eliminate refusal remaining after rank-one editing.
Multilayer ablation improved little over rank-one removal in the original checkpoint.
SAE refusal suppression depended on the model, with one feature dominating Llama.
Extra directions reduced coherence in LLaMA-3.2-1B and were unnecessary in several other models.
A second Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct direction failed to improve refusal suppression beyond a random control.
Affine span-swap effectiveness dropped sharply outside layer 14.
Multidirectional ablation offered little benefit or worsened attack success across several models.
Safety refusal control saturated at one dimension despite multiple effective directions.
One principal direction nearly eliminated Gemma-2-9B-it refusal.
Fine-tuned refusal contrasts remained dominated by one direction.
Random-control adjustment left only small gains from additional visual refusal directions.
False-refusal vectors overlapped safety refusal, and orthogonalized benefits weakened on some unseen prompts.
Affine edits did not consistently outperform linear edits across models.
Broad multidirectional edits incurred capability losses and inconsistently outperformed single-direction editing.
Domain-selective refusal removal generalized poorly across models and still affected non-target domains.
Single-direction ablation met the specified threshold in unmodified Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.
Affine refusal control remained imperfect, with some models resisting every tested approach.
Additional refusal dimensions became weaker, with gains plateauing in Gemma 2 2B.
The shared refusal component drove stronger target jailbreaks than concept-specific residuals.
Learned topic vectors improved refusal selectivity but retained cross-topic leakage.
One refusal vector worked on HarmBench, while reversing combined-intervention order collapsed attack success.
Gabliteration's inconsistent advantage did not establish a benefit from additional directions.
Optimal transport gains largely persisted with one dimension, while one-layer Qwen2.5-32B performance lagged RFA.
Distinct steering directions changed refusal style more than refusal frequency.
Qwen and Gemma showed little separation between over-refusal and harmful-refusal coverage.
Emotion-axis refusal control varied across benchmarks and often coincided with out-of-distribution output.
Multiple directions weakly removed Qwen3-14B refusal; only the leading direction cleanly induced Qwen3-8B refusal.
Category-specific harm signals induced uneven refusal and could act through a shared downstream direction.
A single text direction sufficed to remove Qwen2-VL-2B image refusal.
Mistral-7B-v0.3 refusal was described as essentially one direction.
Primary and secondary refusal effects weakened when ablation used target-layer DCT features.
Category-specific gains varied across models, with DeepSeek retaining a single shared refusal axis.
Qwen2 rank-one recovery exceeded reference-frame subspace recovery, with no observed refusal-direction relocation.
Multi-direction ablation offered small gains under INSEP and no average advantage without the defense.
Extra refusal directions added little in checkpoints already vulnerable to rank-one ablation.
Standard checkpoints concentrated refusal deviation in one direction whose removal already sufficed.
Heterogeneity-aware steering gains were sometimes minimal and sensitive to component selection and covariance modelling.
Held-out prompts retained high refusal, leaving two-direction generalization unresolved.
A single global rank-one edit was reapplied and accepted for Qwen3.5-27B.
One direction eliminated validation refusal after balanced DPO; extra layers offered no clear gain.
Gemma-2-2b showed effective refusal dimension one, with acknowledged layer dependence.
Full INLP erasure offered no consistent improvement over single-direction refusal control.
SmolLM2-1.7B refusal decisions were essentially single-direction, with no advantage from the full probe.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A head-to-head comparison of the affine, cone and dominant-plus-others descriptions on the same models with the same metric.
untested.basis: 'untested parts of V4' lines of arXiv:2411.09003 (only the affine refinement of a single direction), arXiv:2603.04355 (no comparison with affine concept ablation or refusal cones), arXiv:2609.09793 (affine vs cone geometry), arXiv:2605.24583, arXiv:2610.04245, arXiv:2607.02396, arXiv:2604.27019 (no affine or cone test), gh:karpie28 (no comparison; cone procedure not described), lw:ixJrmYrgHM4TenN7D ('Affine vs. cone vs. dominant-plus-others distinctions') and gh:akonpapa (accounts not compared). No support, against or conflict item in either part compares the three on one model. No counts key bears on this.

untested.what: Causal cone tests (gradient-optimized or sampled cones, or ablation and addition along a cone basis) in models above 14B.
untested.basis: The optimized cones of arXiv:2502.17420 cover chat models up to Qwen 2.5 14B (R52). Above 14B, cones are only estimated geometrically (gh:akonpapa r10, Qwen3-VL-30B) or inferred from failed single-direction ablation (arXiv:2609.14759 on GPT-OSS-20B, per its untested line). arXiv:2609.09793 (GLM-5.3-Flash, 320B) lists affine vs cone geometry as untested. counts: V4.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 2; V4.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_size['>100B'] = 1; V4.coverage_by_operation.addition.by_size has no '>100B'.

untested.what: Base (pretrained) models above 8B, and base-vs-instruct comparisons that isolate the number of refusal directions: both checkpoints measured at more than one rank, with repeated runs.
untested.basis: counts: V4.studies_by_stage has no 'base' key, and none of the V4.coverage_by_operation.<operation>.by_stage entries has one. The V4 syntheses and notes name these base-model tests. (1) gh:deepanshumody/increasing-refusal-intervention-robustness#r2: base Llama-3.2-1B needs K=8 iterated ablations to bring harmful refusal below 30%. In this study the instruct model's K=1 holds by construction, because the 30% threshold is the instruct model's own K=1 rate, and no instruct rates at K>1 are reported. (2) arXiv:2610.29555, Table 12 (WildGuard ASR as fractions; RDO-CONE single runs; weighted rank-one WRD-GRPO-IS at alpha=3.0): RDO-CONE 0.953 vs WRD-GRPO-IS 0.93 on Qwen3-8B-Base, 0.865 vs 0.92 on OLMo-3-1025-7B (base), and 0.845 vs 0.93 on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct. The single RDO direction gives 0.34 / 0.61 / 0.40 (Table 1). The authors read weighted rank-one aggregation as competitive with the cone. This study has V4 rows (r52, r54, r56 per the V4 notes; the checker could not find r52/r54 in its pack) but no V4 verdict. Per the notes, its untested line says the comparison does not isolate dimensionality. So base models other than Llama-3.2-1B, and one base-vs-instruct pair (OLMo-3), are tested in the literature; up to 8B, the gap is in the record. ReSAT's 'Base' checkpoints are undefended instruct models (https://openreview.net/forum?id=jDhBl5eznH#A02 and #A16 have stage instruct).

untested.what: Inducing refusal by adding several directions together, or with an affine edit, in models above 10B.
untested.basis: counts: V4.coverage_by_operation.addition.by_size has '1-10B': 9, '10-100B': 1, 'not stated': 1 and no '>100B'. The only 10-100B addition rows in the syntheses steer a single arousal axis on Qwen3-14B (arXiv:2604.03147#r17 to #r23). That text gives no Qwen refusal direction, no angle to one and no random control (Table 10 only). So these rows show an emotion axis steering refusal, not a second direction beside a dominant one. The other addition rows are single-vector steering, with quantitative results only on models under 10B. lw:fSRg5qs9TPbNy3sm5#r1 to #r3 add DCT features or their aggregates toward compliance (jailbreak) on Qwen1.5-7B-Chat. The post also adds DCT features on Qwen1.5-32B-Chat, but only qualitatively and toward compliance. lw:AExopgZ9Yj6qzTrxb steers at one layer in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Adding orthogonalized trust vectors gets responses to harmful prompts (#r1, #r4). Subtracting the compliance vector gives the highest refusal on 100 WildJailBreak adversarial benign prompts in both models (#r6, #r8). Steering against the trust vectors leaves refusal near base (#r7, #r9).

untested.what: Capability or utility retention after SOM multi-direction ablation.
untested.basis: gh:pralab/som-refusal-directions has capability n in its header, and its 'not in rows' line lists capability retention after multi-direction ablation as missing. The MD rows shown for arXiv:2605.21706 report ASR only, and its problems line names capability benchmarks only for CLE-P/CLE-A. No counts key is specific to SOM.

wording_issues.issue: Stated without conditions, but how many directions are needed depends on the model and its training. deepanshumody (one common threshold, 30% harmful refusal): base Llama-3.2-1B needs K=8 (r2), L1+KD needs K=11 (r3) and Cov L2+KD needs K>=16 (r4). For Cov L2+KD, refusal falls from 98% to a minimum of 37% at K=15. Unmodified Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct meets the threshold at K=1 only by construction: the threshold is its own K=1 rate, rounded, and no Instruct rates at K>1 are reported (r1). AebbZlZMxF: standard Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B and Phi-4-mini checkpoints put 0.65-0.80 of the deviation energy on one direction (r40-r45). The participation ratio rises most after DiRe training (4.74-6.25), and other fine-tuned defenses raise it a little: Llama ReFAT 2.04 and ExtRefusal 2.29 against 1.59 original; Mistral ExtRefusal 2.50 against 2.30 (Table 10). ReSAT: the multi-direction gain appears mainly in checkpoints that resist rank-one ablation (A05/A06, A21). It is small or absent in undefended or lightly trained ones (A02, A16); for Llama-3-8B Base this is partly a ceiling, since Single already reaches 92.19 (A02). CARD: the category bank needs 1 component in DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Chat (R7) but 7 in Llama-3.1-8B (R5).

'Better' needs a comparison. Where multi-direction and single-direction removal are compared on one metric, the single direction sometimes matches or nearly matches. INSEP: on undefended bases SOM gives .418 vs .455 for DIM ablation (StrongREJECT harm; verdict reason from Table 11 text). akonpapa: raw ASR is 1.00 for both rank-1 text-only and cross-modal ablation in Qwen2-VL-2B (r5, r7). ReSAT: Llama-3-8B LAT goes 85.16 to 86.72 and ReFAT 89.84 to 92.19 (A04, A10). Many supports are geometric only, with no causal comparison: qRuTqq's domain cosines (r7-r16) and akonpapa's cone energy (r9).

The statement does not say whether it means activation geometry or causal mediation, and the two disagree within single studies. 2604.27019 reports an effective rank of about 1.23-1.27, with k90 = k95 = 1, over raw contrasts stacked across all candidate layers and positions (r24, r25). Yet at R2D2 step 500, ablating a top-3 subspace (built from 5 positions at the selected layer) raises XSTest any-refusal to 0.968, against 0.364 for one direction and 0.228 at baseline (r38, r39). In 2607.14147 the readout looks distributed but one vector acts causally. A full linear probe reads the refuse/comply decision better than the best single direction: AUC 0.848 vs 0.727 on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 0.942 vs 0.847 on Qwen2.5-7B (r42, r44). Under the strong attack, steering d_refuse restores at most 7% refusal at L12 and 0% at L27 (App. H), which the authors read as fitting a distributed decision. But one added plain-minus-attack vector at L12 restores refusal to 74% on held-out prompts, against 0% for random (§4.2; no row). Several supporting results are non-causal: SVD variance shares (2504.18872 r12-r14; the SVD's layer, token position and pair count are not stated) and stable rank (2608.25390 geom_rank7).

The version is named 'More than one direction', but the affine evidence is one direction plus an offset. The untested line of 2411.09003 says only the affine refinement of a single direction is examined. 2603.04355 never tests the mean shift and the variance matching separately, and its component-count results differ by model. On Llama-2-13B, K=1 gives 81.1% ASR vs 82.4% for K=2 (Table 4). On Qwen2.5-14B, K=1 gives 73.6%, K=2 73.0% and K=5 81.8%, with Pile perplexity 19.2 at K=5 (Table 6). In 2605.14347 the full effect needs a move to the benign mean (0.88/0.91), while projecting off the multi-direction span gives 0.00/0.34. No result in part 2 bears on an affine description.

The cone evidence supports only a small, bounded dimension, and much of it is figure-only, inferred or geometric. 2502.17420: cones of up to five dimensions, with lower bounds degrading as dimension grows and a plateau at four in Gemma 2 2B (R51-R53). 2609.14759 infers a cone on GPT-OSS-20B from failed single-direction ablation, with no multi-direction test (R11). karpie28 reports about 50 directions with no procedure (R4). akonpapa's text and image cones are geometric (0.34-0.69 orthogonal energy, r9), and behaviourally a rank-1 text ablation alone removed image refusal (r5).

The 'others' often act only on some prompt types, or are weaker. In 2502.09674, suppressing non-dominant components cuts jailbreak refusal from 96.7% to 14.4%, but plain harmful refusal only from 100% to 80% (r6, r7). That suppression also removes all directions before layer 10, dominant ones included. In 2607.02396, only the first RFM eigenvector induces refusal cleanly (r8-r12). The dominant direction is often not the DiM direction. 2605.24583's untested line says the DiM direction is never ablated. Its Mtemplate top singular vector has |cos| with the Arditi direction of 0.337 (Llama), 0.388 (Gemma) and 0.179 (Qwen), mean over hidden layers, against 0.772/0.860/0.504 for MDiD (Table 4; no row). Ablating Mtemplate u1 alone takes Llama refusal only from 0.97 to 0.84 (r37). Across studies the 'others' are different things: harm categories, token positions, modality, directions that appear after adversarial training, and steering features. CARD fixes the taxonomy (14 BeaverTails categories) and the 90% variance threshold, so its count varies only by model. It ranges from 1 component (DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Chat, R7) through 3 (Gemma-7B, R4) and 6 (Qwen2-1.5B, R8) to 7 (Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B, R5, R6). The authors call Gemma-7B's residual components non-negligible (R4).

Several multi-direction results concern refusal types other than refusing harmful requests. On LLaMA-3.1-8B, over-refusal has cosine 0.41 with the global direction at L17 on the five-task set, and +0.67 on the extended set (2603.27518 R14; Appendix A.4). Knowledge vs safety refusal align at 0.699-0.794 (2609.00760). Non-safety CCN refusals survive safety-direction ablation (2602.02132). General-context instructed refusal is not controlled where safety refusal saturates at k=1 (2610.04245). The untested lines of 2603.27518 and 2609.00760 say that multi-dimensionality within harmful refusal alone is not tested. For 2603.27518 this holds only for causal tests. It has no multi-direction ablation of harmful refusal, but it measures the harmful-refusal direction set representationally: one direction captures 73.5-79.7% of it (Table 8).

Many outcomes offered as evidence are not refusal rates. DCT uses a Sure-minus-Sorry logit difference (r1-r3, r7-r12); its r4-r6 are a feature count and geometry measures on features selected by that score. INSEP uses a StrongREJECT harm score (r13, r14). CARD uses attack success rates of suffix optimization, in which the global and category directions enter only as a projection penalty, with no direction ablation (R9-R11). LoMC uses TCR, the complement of an automated refusal judgment (AB-*-TCR). Several geometry rows measure similarity between DIM vectors, not refusal behaviour.

method_sensitivity.factor: direction source, construction and extraction position
method_sensitivity.what: 2605.24583 ablates only template-matched aligned-minus-base principal components (Mtemplate). It never ablates the MDiD or Arditi direction, so it compares no direction sources. Mtemplate's top singular vector has |cos| 0.337 (Llama), 0.388 (Gemma) and 0.179 (Qwen) with the Arditi direction (MDiD 0.772/0.860/0.504; Table 4). Even so, Gemma-2-9B-it at k=1 drives refusal to a Wilson CI within [0.00, 0.06] (r19). In Llama-3.1-8B, u1 alone gives 0.97 to 0.84 (r37) and narrow-band k=10 gives 0.66 (r22), but wide-band k>=20 gives 0.00 (per the check). 2608.17202: the textbook single-direction derivation worked on gemma-3-27b and Qwen3-14B but not on Qwen3.5-27B or Qwen3.5-9B, where public-recipe or optimizing derivations were needed (R03, R08). gh:irohamca (no V4 verdict): the probe vs diff-of-means cosine is 0.9962 in Qwen-2.5-0.5B-Instruct at the selected layer L12 (r2), but 0.3711 in Gemma-3-1b-it from an earlier single-layer probe at an unstated layer (r4). Both directions contrast a harmful prompt with the same prompt plus 'Sure, here is', not harmful vs harmless. Its verdict notes that a low cosine can arise from activation covariance. 2507.03167: end-of-prompt and CoT-derived directions have generally low cosine, yet both suppress refusal in four reasoning models (r26, figure only).

method_sensitivity.factor: what set of vectors is decomposed when measuring dimensionality
method_sensitivity.what: On the same model, the measured rank depends on what is stacked. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: the deviation matrix over a 0.4-0.8 depth band has participation ratio 1.59 and leading-direction energy 0.79 (AebbZlZMxF r40, r41), while CARD's stacked category-direction bank at layer 15 needs 7 components for 90% of variance (R5). Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3: PR 2.30 and T1 0.65 (r42, r43) vs 7 components (R6). Llama-2-7B-chat (baseline SSFT variant): SVD of harmful-minus-harmless activation differences gives a first component of 49.43% and a second of 4.76% (2504.18872 r8, r9). The text gives no layer, token position or pair count for this SVD; layer 14 and 100 pairs describe the direction computation. Five harm-domain DIM directions in the same model have pairwise cosines 0.3214-0.7885 (qRuTqq r8-r17), and the text says three PCs explain 90% (r18), without saying what the PCA was run on.

method_sensitivity.factor: operation: inducing refusal (addition or steering) vs removing it (ablation)
method_sensitivity.what: 2610.04245: safety refusal is controlled at k=1 by both addition (R1-R5) and ablation (R6-R9). The two operations differ only for Llama-3.1-8B general-context refusal: additive steerability saturates beyond k=3 (K-Means; R10), while ablation is ineffective in all four settings up to k=5 (R11). 2607.02396 (Qwen3 8B): only the first RFM eigenvector induces refusal cleanly under steering (r8-r12). Under the ablation weight edit, ASR is 0.20 ± 0.04 at k=1, 0.62 ± 0.01 at k=3 and 0.73 ± 0.03 at k=5, against a vanilla 0.00 ± 0.00 (Table 1; r3, r5). 2502.17420 (not in rows; Appendix E, Fig. 18, Qwen 2.5): cone directions still induce refusal under addition at higher dimensions than under ablation. 2602.02132: distinct per-split directions give near-identical RR/ORR under steering at the selected, near-saturating alpha (Table 1; st-g-hum). Under ablation they differ widely: Table 2 de-refusal is 0.0-14.1% (Gemma), 0.9-73.5% (Qwen) and 14.1-39.1% (Llama).

method_sensitivity.factor: layer, layer band and number of intervention layers
method_sensitivity.what: 2603.04355 (LlamaGuard ASR %, HarmBench test set): on Qwen2.5-32B, one-layer PCA-OT gives 45.75 and two-layer PCA-OT 75.94, against 57.55 for RFA (r23, r24). On Llama-2-13B, PCA-OT at layer 5 gives 0.6, against a no-intervention 1.26 (Table 1; r50). 2411.09003: a poor layer choice gives no effect or nonsense. The useful region lies around the model midpoint (layer 15 for Llama 3 8B). CARD (method line): the best layer varies by category (L15, L17, L20, L22). On a Qwen2-1.5B scan (300 held-out mixed-category prompts), layer means range from 40.20% to 45.00% ASR and layer 20 is best, while the main runs use layer 15. qRuTqq (method line): the best layer was 12 for safety-related and 13 for policy-related prompts, and 10-12 in the five-domain experiment.

deepanshumody (iterated Arditi-style ablation): pushing harmful refusal below 30% needs K=8 on base Llama-3.2-1B, K=11 after L1+KD and K>=16 after Cov L2+KD (r2-r4). For Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, K=1 holds by construction: the 30% threshold is Instruct's own K=1 rate, and no Instruct rates at K>1 are reported (r1). method_sensitivity.factor: coherence filtering, unfinished outputs and judge
method_sensitivity.what: 2609.14759 (GPT-OSS-20B): CoT-mean ablation removes refusal in 88% of cases, but that 88% counts incoherent generations. It is the rate before the coherence filter, which excludes exactly those cases. The end-of-prompt direction gives 4% coherent flips (R11, R13). 2609.09793: the lowest judged refusal, 0.200 at rank 8, comes with 0.164 of replies unfinished, and 0.205 are unfinished at rank 10 (r42, r44). AebbZlZMxF: rank-16 SVD retention counts only coherent outputs, so survivorship bias applies (r31). 2604.03147: arousal-axis steering of Qwen3-8B at alpha=+3 gives 17% out-of-distribution generation (r16). The check finds no Qwen refusal-direction comparison, so this row is coverage, not a V4 test.

2604.03147 (arousal-axis steering, HarmBench refusal): Qwen needs about 7 times the Llama strength (|alpha| up to 3.0, against up to 0.45). At |alpha|<=1.0, Qwen refusal stays at 87.0-91.5%. The no-intervention baseline is 0.192% (simplified template) or 0.00% (official). 97.88% equals the simplified-template DBDI figure. 2.11% equals the Refusal-Only simplified AdvBench figure, which may be a coincidence or a copy error.

Under the cross-dataset protocol, the calibration set differs by test benchmark and is not stated per column, so the benchmark effect may be confounded with calibration. 2602.02132 (gemma-2-9b-it; baseline RR 1.00, ORR 0.00 by construction): projecting out a safety-derived direction gives RR 0.00 on CrimeAssistance-SB (ab-g-crime) but 0.45 on Humanizing-CCN (ab-g-hum). 2607.02714 (Kimi K2, cybersecurity-direction edit): misinformation refusal goes from 100% to 88% on the 306-prompt cross-evaluation set (r4), and from 98% to 74% on the 360-prompt scientific benchmark (r12).
